parsed_answer.content:
Spring Boot 3 introduces Ahead-Of-Time (AOT) compilation, a transformative capability that fundamentally shifts how enterprise Java applications transition from source code to execution. Traditionally, the Spring framework relies heavily on dynamic runtime behavior: classpath scanning, runtime bean definition registration, extensive use of Java Reflection, and dynamic proxy generation via CGLIB or JDK proxies upon application startup. While this runtime flexibility allows for powerful dependency injection and auto-configuration, it incurs a heavy startup latency penalty and a bloated memory footprint due to the metadata required by the JVM to support these dynamic features at runtime.

Spring Boot 3 AOT compilation solves this problem by shifting these expensive operations from runtime to build-time. During the Maven or Gradle build phase, the Spring AOT engine analyzes the application context, inspects bean definitions, resolves conditional annotations, and generates native source code and resource configurations. This generated code eliminates the need for dynamic runtime classpath scanning and heavy reflection. When paired with GraalVM Native Image technology, this AOT-processed output is compiled directly into a platform-specific machine code binary. The resulting native executable bypasses the HotSpot JVM startup phase, removes the JIT compilation warm-up period, and slashes memory consumption by eliminating the metadata caches traditionally maintained by the JVM heap for class loading and reflection.

items: Closed-World Assumption: GraalVM Native Image operates under a closed-world assumption, meaning all classes, methods, and fields reachable by the application must be known at build time. Anything invoked dynamically via reflection must be explicitly registered.

Runtime Hints API: Spring Boot 3 introduces the RuntimeHints API. Framework components and developer code use this API to programmatically register reflection, resource loading, serialization, and proxy requirements for build-time processing.

Generated Component Registry: The AOT engine produces replacements for standard Spring factories, such as BeanFactoryInitializationAdapters, which statically configure beans without reflective instantiation.
GraalVM Reachability Metadata: Spring Boot auto-configures vast sets of reflection hints out-of-the-box for popular libraries, leveraging the centralized GraalVM reachability metadata repository.

parsed_answer.content: Production Gotcha: The most common failure mode when adopting Spring Boot 3 AOT and Native Images is the 'ClassNotFoundException' or 'NoSuchMethodException' at runtime, triggered by libraries using unhindered reflection or ServiceLoader mechanisms. Because the JVM heap does not lazily load classes the same way under native compilation, missing reflection hints will cause immediate application failure during startup. Always thoroughly test native executables using integration tests executed via the native-maven-plugin.

title: What is Spring Boot 3 AOT compilation?
